title: Re-Read Yield and Insight Density
dataSources: Reading progress (`reading:progress`), highlights (`highlight:capture`), note links (`note:link`), books finished (`book:finished`).
app: Reading and knowledge-management telemetry — Goodreads / StoryGraph libraries, Kindle highlights (Readwise), and note-graph exports (Obsidian, Notion) — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=book:finished reread=yes
| stats avg(highlights_count) as avg_highlights, avg(notes_created) as avg_notes, count as rereads by author
| eval insight_density=round(avg_notes/avg_highlights,2)
| sort - insight_density
description: Shows whether rereading specific authors or categories produces more notes and insights the second time around.
value: Some books repay rereading far better than others; insight density helps you choose where a reread is worth the time.
implementation: Flag rereads in `book:finished` and compare average highlights and notes created by author.
visualization: Bar chart of insight density for reread authors.
grandmaExplanation: It spots which rereads give you the most useful ideas instead of just repeating what you already knew.
